messages:
maya: Heads-up — trying to bring up hf/artemis-13b for Redwood serving. Model repo uses custom classes (CustomCausalLM) and the HF package insists on trust_remote_code=true. auto_map import fails when we try to convert.
sam: can you paste the exact error? stacktrace?
maya: pasted below:
```
ValueError: Model class CustomCausalLM not found in transformers library.
Please set trust_remote_code=True or provide a custom model class.
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ImportError: Cannot auto_map model architecture -> AutoModelForCausalLM import failed.
```
liam: ok that's the expected behavior for repos with custom architecture. Two options: (1) set trust_remote_code=True when loading (2) implement a shim CustomCausalLM in our conversion path. Both have pros/cons.
jyoti: trust_remote_code is risky for hosted/dedicated unless we sandbox. For Private we could allow it with extra policy. Also saw tokenizer issues: special tokens absent and chat_template.json refers to <|system|> token which isn't in tokenizer.json.
maya: tokenizer_config.json from repo:
```
{"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}
```
but the repo's chat template includes <|system|> and <|assistant|> placeholders — mismatch causes generation to emit raw tokens and break role parsing.
liam: that explains the QA regression we saw earlier. model-onboard-bot: eval run complete (dev/regression-suite):
- baseline unquantized (hosted): EM on SQuAD-like set = 82.3
- 8-bit LLM.int8() run: EM = 80.1
- 4-bit QAT/LLM.int4 equivalent: EM = 73.8 (major drop)
- latency (tokens/s): unquantized=220 tok/s, int8=340 tok/s, int4=480 tok/s
- sample failure mode: replies include raw token ids when tokenizer missing special tokens.
maya: interesting: 8-bit looks fine, 4-bit introduces semantics drift. Might be quantization amplitude/ln scaling bug with custom attention.
sam: did we enable skip_special_tokens on decode? also check tokenizers v0.13 vs v0.15 compatibility — repo uses older huggingface tokenizer code.
jyoti: I ran quick convert with trust_remote_code=True in a sandbox and added a small token map: {"<|system|>": "<s>", "<|assistant|>": "</s>"} — fixed a lot of the role parsing, but the 4-bit hallucination/regression persisted. My hypothesis: custom attention kernel uses ops that don't quantize well; our quant kernels choose wrong clipping/scale heuristics.
liam: action items we discussed: 1) maya to prepare a minimal shim that exposes standard AutoModelForCausalLM API mapping to repo CustomCausalLM (safe surface), 2) jyoti to run per-layer sensitivity analysis for 4-bit quant and dump activation distributions, 3) sam to update conversion logs to detect chat_template vs tokenizer mismatch and auto-suggest token map, 4) decide trust_remote_code policy per deployment tier.
maya: I'll throw up a draft PR with shim + unit tests (quick smoke: full convo roundtrip). Also include a conversion flag --force-token-map to inject remapped special tokens during conversion.
sam: for metrics, can we add a targeted QA eval and a small dialogue-turn consistency test in the eval harness? so quant regressions are caught earlier.
model-onboard-bot: noted. Scheduled a canary run for next nightly: artemis-13b (shim + token-map) on: dedicated-qual with int8 and int4. Will post results in this thread.
maya: thanks — leaning toward blocking 4-bit for hosted until we understand attention kernel mismatch. Int8 seems like good tradeoff.
